title: WPSS/1913/2016 of Bhaskar Sharma Vs State Of Uttarakhand AND OTHERS

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition (S/S) No. 1913 of 2016

Versus
State of Uttarakhand & others Ö.ÖRespondents
Present:- Mr. Sandeep Tiwari, Advocate, present for the petitioner.
 Mr. Vikas Pandey, Brief Holder, present for the State of
 Uttarakhand/respondent Nos.1 to 3.
 Mr. Lalit Samant, Advocate, present for the respondent Nos.4 & 5.
Honíble Sudhanshu Dhulia, J. (Oral)
 The petitioner was a candidate for the post of
Lecturer (Sociology), for which the post was advertised by
Inter College, Algada, District - Pithoragarh. Admittedly,
certain preferential marks were given to the candidate in
the selection process, who has got teaching experience,
however, the teaching experience certificate was to be given
by the school concerned where the teaching has been
imparted by the candidate and it was to be duly
countersigned by the Block Education Officer and the Chief
Education Officer. The experience certificate of the
petitioner though was signed by the Block Education
Officer but was not signed by the Chief Education Officer
as according to the petitioner, the concerned Chief
Education Officer at the relevant time was on leave. Since
the preferential marks were not added to the portfolio of the
petitioner, his name initially did not figure amongst the
first 18 candidates, while calling for the interview. Hence,
the petitioner constrained to file present writ petition.
2. By an interim order of this Court dated
23.09.2016, the petitioner was permitted to appear in the
selection process. Meanwhile, he has also submitted his
experience certificate, which was duly signed by the Chief
Education Officer. The selection process has already taken
place and the result is with the Chief Education Officer in a
sealed cover.

2
3. In the counter affidavit, the Committee of
Management, Inter College Algada, District Pithoragarh has
raised objection that the mandatory condition of the
advertisement was that duly certified experience certificate
shall be filed before the last date, which was 30.10.2015.
Since this was the mandatory condition, the petitioner did
not fulfill the mandatory condition and, therefore, the
candidature of the petitioner was not liable to be
considered.
4. This objection of the respondents has no
relevance, inasmuch as, the objection raised at the hands
of the respondents is merely technical in nature.
5. The case of the petitioner is that he was
genuinely handicapped in submitting the relevant
experience certificate as the Chief Education Officer could
not countersign it as at the relevant time he was on leave
and the Block Education Officer refused to countersign as
he was the Member of the Selection Committee. This
certificate has now been duly signed by the Chief
Education Officer and subject to the veracity of the
certificate, the candidature of the petitioner is liable to be
considered.
6. In view of the aforesaid, writ petition is
allowed. Let the experience certificate of the petitioner be
verified and the veracity of the same must be examined by
the Chief Education Officer or District Education Officer, as
the case might be. It is further directed considering the
case of the petitioner, the result of the same be declared
and the appointment letter be issued as expeditiously as
possible to the selected candidates.
